question: Given a predicted set of the top 50 differentially expressed genes from a cancer versus normal RNA-seq analysis and a reference set of 30 known oncogenes from the COSMIC database, compute and report the intersection size and Jaccard score between the two gene sets.

files.eval_guideline: Intersection count must match the reference exactly; Jaccard score must match within +/-0.001; row order and header labels may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename jaccard_score.csv and matching CSV format. They correspond to the same task of reporting the intersection size and Jaccard score for the DEG and COSMIC oncogene sets.

parameters.question: Compare the reported gene-set intersection count and Jaccard score. Require the intersection count to match exactly and the Jaccard score to match within +/-0.001, allowing different row order and header labels.

files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires value-by-value comparison of two deterministic metrics while allowing structural differences. Approximate comparison accommodates row and header differences while enforcing the exact intersection count and specified Jaccard tolerance.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables use the same Metric and Value columns and require no transpose. Metric uniquely identifies summary rows. Normalize candidate Intersection_Size to reference Intersection, then match that row and Jaccard_Score, excluding the three additional set-size metrics. These summary metrics are unordered despite the task mentioning top 50 genes. Compare intersection exactly and Jaccard within 0.001; both reported values match.

column_configs.name: Value
column_configs.reasoning: Value is float64 and contains the required intersection count and Jaccard score. Assuming RAE = absolute error / absolute reference value, 0.001 / 0.2308 gives the relative tolerance for Jaccard. This also rejects any integer intersection count other than 15, though fractional count discrepancies require a separate exact check.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: Exclude Metric because it is used only for alignment. Compare the intersection and jaccard_score rows; exclude rows with reference NaN because their auxiliary metrics are unspecified and not required. Use numerical RAE because numerical agreement matters. The candidate matches both required reference values. The schema permits only one tolerance for Value, so it cannot fully express exact intersection equality alongside a Jaccard absolute tolerance of 0.001: enforce intersection equality separately if fractional counts are possible. Row order and header differences are handled by alignment.
